advisory.summary: A company owner could read a user belonging to another company through GET /api/v1/users/{id}, because the view check tested only that the caller owned the company named in the header, not that the target belonged to it.
note: UserPolicy::view on 2.4.0 returns $user->isOwner() alone. isOwner() is
true when the caller owns the company in the `company` header, so an
owner of company A reads a user of company B by naming A in the header:
GET /api/v1/users/{id} loads the target by global id. 2.4.1 adds
sharesActiveCompany($model) and answers 403 when the target does not
Measured by hand on both tags before this pair was written. Attacker is
the seeded admin, owner of company A; victim owns company B and belongs to
B only. Attacker (header A) GET /api/v1/users/{victim}: 200 with the
marker in name and email on 2.4.0, 403 with no marker on 2.4.1. Victim
(header B) reading its own record is 200 with the marker on both, which is
the control and the marker probe. A fabricated Bearer token is 401 on
both tags, so the attacker's 403 on 2.4.1 is a live credential refused,
not a dead session or a removed route.

checks.name: A company owner must not read a user who belongs only to another company
